title: Granudacyn Peritoneal Lavage in Children Undergoing Laparoscopic Appendectomy for Complicated Appendicitis
official: Prospective Longitudinal Single-Center Cohort Study of Granudacyn Use for Peritoneal Lavage During Laparoscopic Appendectomy for Complicated Appendicitis in Children
summary: Complicated appendicitis in children can lead to postoperative infections, including intra-abdominal abscess. This prospective observational cohort study will describe clinical outcomes in children undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy for complicated appendicitis at AOU Meyer IRCCS, Florence, Italy, when peritoneal lavage includes Granudacyn as part of routine clinical care. The primary outcome is the incidence of clinically significant intra-abdominal abscess within 30 days after surgery. Postoperative complications, pain, analgesic use, length of stay, recovery, and possible adverse events will also be assessed. Outcomes will be compared exploratorily with historical cases treated without Granudacyn.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Age 0-17 years
* Urgent or delayed urgent laparoscopic appendectomy
* Intraoperative diagnosis of gangrenous appendicitis or perforated appendicitis with localized or diffuse purulent peritonitis and/or intra-abdominal abscess
* Laparoscopic completion with peritoneal lavage is feasible
* Written informed consent from a parent or legal guardian

Exclusion Criteria

* Uncomplicated appendicitis without gangrene or perforation
* Generalized fecal peritonitis or septic shock requiring immediate deviation from the planned laparoscopic approach or primary conversion to open surgery
* Known allergy or contraindication to any Granudacyn component
* Pre-existing severe renal or hepatic impairment, or another condition considered by the clinician to substantially increase the risk of irrigation-related adverse events
* Participation in an interventional study that could interfere with study outcomes
* Placement of an intra-abdominal drain at the end of surgery
